ev.q: CDC analyzed state and area data from the 2006 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS) survey.
In 2006, the median prevalence of current cigarette smoking among adults in the 50 states and DC was 20.2%
In 2006, the median percentage of ever smokers aged 18--35 years who had quit was 34.0% for the 50 states and DC
the median prevalence of current cigarette smoking among adults in the 50 states and DC was 20.2%
The states with the highest percentages of ever smokers who had quit in this age group were Utah (47.9%) and Minnesota (43.7%).
Utah and USVI were the only areas to achieve the Healthy People 2010 objective to reduce overall adult smoking prevalence to < 12%
BRFSS is a state-based, random-digit--dialed telephone survey of the noninstitutionalized, U.S. civilian population
CDC analyzed state and area data from the 2006 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS) survey.

methods_quotes.q: Estimates were weighted by age and sex distributions of each state or area population.
Because BRFSS data are state-specific, national median prevalences are reported instead of national averages.
The percentage of ever smokers who had quit smoking was calculated by dividing the number of former smokers by the number of ever smokers.
Sample sizes were too small (i.e., <50 respondents) for meaningful analysis.
